summary: Unnikrishnan Payyappallimana is an Indologist who studied at Bharathiar University and the University of Amsterdam. He held posts at the Foundation for the Revitalization of Local Health Traditions, Amala Institute of Medical Sciences, and the University of Toyama.

Unrai Wogihara (1869–1937) was an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Junjirō Takakusu and Ernst Leumann, completing his degree at Strasbourg. He taught at the University of Tokyo, Shukyo University, Shiba High School, and Taisho University.
Unshō Shaku (1827–1909) was a Buddhist and religious studies scholar who studied at Mount Koya in 1844. He taught Ekai Kawaguchi and founded both the Juzen-kai in 1884 and the Kairitsu Gakkō.

Uranchimeg B. Ujeed specializes in Buddhist and Iranian and Central Asian studies. She earned her Ph.D. from SOAS University of London and served as a Research Associate in the Mongolia and Inner Asia Unit at the University of Cambridge.

Uranchimeg Tsultem, a scholar of Buddhist studies, tibetology, and art history, earned her Ph.D. from UC Berkeley. She held positions at the Mongolian State University of Arts and Culture, National University of Mongolia, and Indiana University Indianapolis.

Urs App (born 1949) specializes in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and Japanology. He studied under Richard DeMartino, Yoshitaka Iriya, and Seizan Yanagida, earning a Ph.D. from Temple University, and was associate director at Hanazono University's International Research Institute for Zen Buddhism.

Ute Hüsken (born 1965) is an Indologist and scholar of religious and Buddhist studies. She earned her doctorate under Heinz Bechert at Göttingen and completed her habilitation at Heidelberg, holding professorships at the University of Oslo and Heidelberg University.

Utz Podzeit (1942–2022) was an Austrian Indologist who completed his Dr. phil. at the University of Vienna. He served as a university lecturer at Vienna's Indology institute from 1969 and conducted research at the University of Madras (1972–1974).

V. Raghavan (1908–1979) was an Indian Indologist. He earned his Ph.D. under S. Kuppuswami Sastri at the University of Madras, where he served in the Sanskrit Department from 1934 to 1968, and founded the Kuppuswami Sastri Research Institute.

V. Venkatachalam (1925–2002) was an Indologist educated at Madras and Nagpur universities. He directed the Scindia Oriental Research Institute and the Bhogilal Leherchand Institute of Indology, served as vice-chancellor of Sampurnanand Sanskrit University, and chaired the ICPR.
V. Venkayya (1864–1912) was a scholar in Indology and history and archaeology. He was educated at Madras Christian College and the University of Madras, and succeeded Eugen Hultzsch.
Vaibhav Singh is a scholar of Indology who earned his PhD from the University of Reading in 2017. He held a post at the University of Reading, attested in 2018.

Valdo H. Viglielmo (1926–2016) was a scholar of Japanology and philosophy who studied at Harvard, Pennsylvania, Tokyo, and Gakushuin. He taught at Harvard, several Tokyo universities, and Princeton, before serving as a professor at the University of Hawaiʻi (1965–2002).
Valeria Gazizova is a scholar in tibetology and religious studies who completed her Master's thesis at the University of Oslo under the supervision of Per Kværne (attested 2009).

Van Austin Harvey (1926–2021) was a religious studies and philosophy scholar who earned degrees from Occidental, Yale, and Princeton Seminary. He chaired programs at Southern Methodist University and the University of Pennsylvania, and was a professor at Stanford University.

Vans Kennedy (1784–1846) was an Indologist and linguist. He served as judge-advocate-general in the Bombay Army from 1817 to 1835 and later served as president of the Asiatic Society of Mumbai from approximately 1835 to 1846.

Vasily Mikhaylovich Alekseyev (1881–1951) was a Russian Sinologist who studied at St. Petersburg University and under Édouard Chavannes. He served at Saint Petersburg State University, the Institute of Oriental Studies of the Russian Academy of Sciences, and the National Library.

Vasily Pavlovich Vasilyev (1818–1900) was a scholar in Sinology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. He studied at Kazan Federal University under Józef Szczepan Kowalewski and served as a professor at Kazan and later at Saint Petersburg State University.

Vasily Seseman (1884–1963) was a philosopher who studied at Saint Petersburg State University (1903–1909). He held academic posts at Saint Petersburg State University (1915–1918), Vytautas Magnus University (1923–1940), and Vilnius University (1940–1950).

Vasudev Vishnu Gokhale (1901–1996) was a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and Sinology who earned his PhD from the University of Bonn in 1930. He held faculty posts at Fergusson College, Visva-Bharati University, and the University of Delhi.
